meta.title: Warrior data sheet for WoW Forever (level 60, vs level 63 training dummy): Fury (dual wield), Arms (two-hand), Protection (tank)
meta.scope: Rage rules (normalized outgoing rage, incoming rage), every ability a level-60 warrior uses against a raid boss, stances, procs and passives, everything needed to make a dummy that attacks a tank, talent trees, the sims' builds, priority lists and default stats.
meta.howToRead: Every number is an object {value, unit, source, confidence, note}. 'source' is a GitHub permalink (repo@commit/path#Lline), a URL, or a list of them. 'confidence' is one of the three values in confidenceLegend.

confidenceLegend.confirmed-forever: Stated by Forever client data (spell rows, talent curves, Wowhead Forever tooltips), by Blizzard, or measured in game on the beta. Most beta measurements were taken at levels 8-30; level-60 values are datamined or extrapolated unless noted.
confidenceLegend.sim-provisional: A modelling choice of one or both sims with no Forever source yet, or where the two sims disagree. Use it, but expect it to change.
confidenceLegend.classic-fallback: Forever data is silent, so the sims keep the Classic 1.12 / Classic Era value.

simsCompared.gs: gunba/wow-forever-sim (branch 'forever'), commit 9c05fc890b (2026-10-09). Engine: wowsims/classic + ElliotWood/Forever. Uses the current (post-1-October) talent tree.
simsCompared.fs: laurencestokes/foreversim (branch 'master'), commit 255df1627f (2026-10-01). Engine: wowsims/forever. Carries the beta client spell rows (sim/core/spelldata/spells_auto_gen.go). Its warrior talent tree and crit-rage rule predate the 1 October Fury/Protection rework.

practiceYardSummary: White-hit rage is a fixed amount per landed swing: 3.46 x weapon speed (one-hand main hand), 4.5 x speed (two-hander), half of the one-hand rate for the off hand. Damage does not matter. Crits give +100%. Misses, dodges and parries give 0.
Rage from damage taken is small in Forever: about 6 rage per landed hit of a 3,000-base level-63 boss (Classic about 17).
GCD is 1.5 s for all warrior abilities. Heroic Strike/Cleave are on-next-swing (off GCD) and the swing they replace gives no rage.
Protection needs a dummy that hits back: blocks, dodges and parries enable Revenge and generate rage (Shield Specialization, Master of Defense).

rage.headline: Forever 'fully normalized' white-hit rage: each landed auto attack gives a fixed amount set by the weapon's listed speed and hand, independent of damage. It is not TBC's formula (TBC kept a damage term plus a hit factor); it resembles Cataclysm/MoP normalized rage, with a separate higher two-hand rate.

maxRage.note: Measured cap 100 (magey #3). Boundless Rage (+rage cap) was removed on 1 October, so 100 is the only cap.

practiceYard.note: gs's DPS preset starts at 50 rage (ui/warrior/presets.ts L97-102, assumes pre-pull Bloodrage/Charge); tank presets and fs start at 0.

blizzardStatement.value: Rage from dealing damage is fully normalized: rage gained is based on the speed of the weapon that dealt the damage. Critical strikes re-added (+75% on 30 Sep, raised to +100% on 1 Oct).

blizzardStatements.value: 30 Sep: 'We kept the original formula for Rage generation from taking damage, but ... Rage gain from damage is calculated by ignoring Armor ... as if you always had 50% damage reduction from Armor. Rage gain also ignores all damage absorption effects.'
blizzardStatements.source: https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/news/24301514 (Blizzard, WoW Forever Class Deep Dives: Priest and Warrior, 30 Sep 2026)

blizzardStatements.value: 8 Oct: the calculation now uses an expected creature's health instead of the player's health (more Stamina no longer lowers rage); critical strikes and crushing blows now raise rage correctly; absorbs are ignored; rage is balanced around 20%-40% armor varying by level instead of 50%. 'The typical Warrior or Druid should be gaining more Rage from taking damage.'

preFixMeasurement.value: rage = preArmorDamage x 10 / playerMaxHealth (geared, levels 8-9); doubled below ~130-170 armor; misses, dodges, parries give nothing; a blocked hit gives the rage of the unblocked amount; attacker level did not matter
preFixMeasurement.note: Measured before the 8 Oct fix (which replaced player health by expected creature health). Valid only as historical evidence of the shape.

expectedCreatureStatsLevel60.note: Client ExpectedStat table (build 1.60.1.70291). Reference armor = 3566/(3566+5500) = 39.3%, inside Blizzard's '20%-40%'. Which level's row the server uses (player or creature) is unknown.

gsModel.note: Explicitly unverified scenario. Keeps actual armor, Defensive Stance and block in the damage (so more armor = less rage, unlike Blizzard's 30 Sep wording). Crits/crushes count through their larger damage. Periodic damage gives no rage. gs tested coefficient 20 as an alternative.

fsModel.value: rage = preArmorDamage x 10 / playerMaxHealth (only landed hits)
fsModel.note: The pre-8-October measured formula; superseded by Blizzard's fix.

blizzardTextReading.value: rage = preArmorDamage (x2 crit, x1.5 crush; absorbs and the blocked amount ignored) x (1 - 0.39334) x C / 4365, C unknown (10 matches the gs coefficient; 20 would reproduce the old '50% armor' calibration)
source: https://worldofwarcraft.blizzard.com/en-us/news/24301514 (Blizzard, WoW Forever Class Deep Dives: Priest and Warrior, 30 Sep 2026)
blizzardTextReading.note: Our reading of 'ignore armor' + 'expected creature health' + '20-40% reference armor'. Not a sim formula.

recommendedForPracticeYard.value: ragePerLandedHit = C x rawHit x (1 - 0.3933) / 4365 with C = 10, rawHit = boss damage before armor, block and stance, after the crit (x2) / crush (x1.5) multiplier; give 0 for misses, dodges, parries; give full rage for blocked hits
recommendedForPracticeYard.note: With the gs default boss (avg raw hit 4,475) this is about 6.2 rage per landed normal hit, 12.4 per crit, 9.3 per crushing blow; the gs model gives about 6.4 for a 7,858-armor tank in Defensive Stance, so both readings agree for a typical tank. Expose C as a setting (10-20).

classicForComparison.value: rage = 2.5 x damageTaken / 243.6 (rage conversion of the level-63 attacker), i.e. 1 rage per ~97 damage after armor
classicForComparison.note: About 17 rage per post-armor boss hit of 1,700. Forever pays roughly a third of that.

openQuestions: Level-60 white rage: are 3.46 (one-hand) and 4.5 (two-hand) per second of speed still exact at 60? Measured only at levels 8-22.
Crit rage after 1 October: x2 for every white crit (gs) or 'add the base once' (measured on the 30 Sep build: one-hander x2, two-hander x1.77)? Does the off hand get it?
Dual Wield Specialization off-hand rage: +10%/point (gs client curve) or +5%/point (Wowhead tooltip) or none?
Incoming rage: coefficient (10 or 20), whether actual armor is ignored (Blizzard 30 Sep text) or kept (gs model), which level's expected health the server uses, and whether DoT damage gives rage.
Berserker Rage: size of the extra incoming rage (gs keeps +2 per landed melee hit).
Out-of-combat rage decay rate and delay (Lingering Rage adds 2-10 s).
Attack-power shares the client does not carry: Rend (fs 2% AP/tick), Thunder Clap (fs 2.55% AP), Revenge (fs 25% AP); gs uses none.
Threat values: Revenge (gs x2.25 + 270 vs fs damage + 120), Thunder Clap (x2.5 vs x1), Shield Slam (+508), Heroic Strike (+173), Cleave (+100), Sunder's AP term, Demoralizing Shout per-target amount.
Base Slam swing reset: gs never resets the swing in Forever, Blizzard and fs say base Slam interrupts it until Improved Slam.
Flurry charge rules (yellow crits, queued attacks, both hands) and whether hasted swings keep full rage at 60 (yes at low level).
Unbridled Wrath: has the 1 October proc-rate fix (12%/point) reached live builds?
Bloodthrill proc rate: 4%/point (Blizzard 24 Sep, gs) vs 15% shown by Wowhead.
Availability at launch of AQ-era book ranks: Heroic Strike 9 (+157), Revenge 6 (138-168), Battle Shout 7 (140 AP). Fallbacks: HS 8 (+138), Revenge 5 (109-133), Battle Shout 6 (111).
GCD of Shield Wall (client 1.5 s, gs none) and Concussion Blow; Sweeping Strikes duration 20 s (client) vs 10 s (gs).
Dual-wield white miss penalty (19%) unmeasured; glancing damage ~25% reduction in the beta (bug?) vs 35% intended; are specials still two-roll for crit?
Real Forever boss swing damage and speed (3,000-base 2.0 s swing is a gs stress assumption).
Is the dummy stun-immune (Concussion Blow, Charge/Intercept stuns)?
Off-hand crit attribution for Deep Wounds (main-hand payload in both sims) and Weaponmaster's off-hand mace armor ignore.
Extra attacks (Weaponmaster sword, Windfury): do they give rage like normal swings?
Does a target's block of the warrior's swing still give white rage (sims: yes)?
